citation: PMID 11274162 (Russnak et al. 2001, J Biol Chem)
claim_tested: AVT2 differs from vacuolar paralogs in localization/sorting
key_finding: AVT1 imports large neutral aa into vacuole; AVT3/AVT4/AVT6 export aa from vacuole; UniProt traces the vacuole-membrane assignment of AVT2, AVT1, AVT5 and AVT7 to this single paper
context: S. cerevisiae, isolated vacuoles + GFP fusions
confidence_limitations: High for AVT1/3/4/6 transport. AVT2 localization is supported but AVT2 transport activity was not demonstrated.

claim_tested: [DE]xxxL[LI] is required for AP-3 vacuolar sorting in yeast
key_finding: Yeast AP-3 cargo ALP/Pho8 is sorted by Leu13/Val14 in residues 1-16 of its cytosolic tail; that tail has no [DE]xxxL[LI] match
context: S. cerevisiae, ALP-GDPase chimeras, clathrin-ts and AP-3 mutants
confidence_limitations: High. One cargo, but it is the defining cargo of the yeast ALP/AP-3 pathway.

citation: PMID 9722605 (Darsow, Burd & Emr 1998, J Cell Biol)
claim_tested: Acidic dileucine signals operate in yeast AP-3 sorting
key_finding: A 7-residue acidic di-leucine region in Vam3 is required for AP-3-dependent sorting; recovered by our regex as EQSPLL(155)
confidence_limitations: High. Shows the motif class is real in yeast, which validates the scan but not its absence-based use.

key_finding: [DE]xxxL[LI] is recognized by AP-1, AP-2, AP-3 and AP-4, so a hit is not AP-3 specific
CLN3 uses a non-canonical EEEX(8)LI acidic-cluster dileucine; under this relaxed pattern AVT2 scores 2 N-tail hits vs 0 for AVT1/AVT5/AVT6/AVT7
confidence_limitations: Heterologous system; our relaxed scan is pattern-matching only, no binding data.

citation: PMID 14691137 (Janvier et al. 2003, J Cell Biol)
key_finding: Nef and LIMP-II [DE]xxxL[LI] signals bind AP-1 gamma-sigma1 and AP-3 delta-sigma3; our scan recovers LIMP-2 ERAPLI(471)
confidence_limitations: Positive control for the scan only.

citation: This work: UniProt P39981/P47082/P36062/P50944/P38176/P40074/P40501 feature + sequence scan
claim_tested: Vacuolar AVT paralogs carry [DE]xxxL[LI] in cytosolic tails while AVT2 does not
key_finding: 0/7 paralogs have [DE]xxxL[LI] in either terminal tail; 0/7 have KKxx or KxKxx; AVT5/6/7 N-tails are only 6-7 aa
context: S. cerevisiae S288C canonical UniProt sequences; TM spans are ECO:0000255 predictions
confidence_limitations: Tail boundaries depend on predicted TM spans. Interhelical loops were not scanned as cytosolic tails per the specified protocol.

citation: This work: Smith-Waterman alignment of AVT2 vs paralogs
claim_tested: AVT2 has a genuine N-terminal cytosolic extension
key_finding: AVT2 conserved core starts at residue 67, aligning to residue 3 of AVT5/AVT6; AVT2 therefore has a real ~66-aa acidic, Ser/Thr-rich N-extension absent from AVT5/6/7
confidence_limitations: Low sequence identity; alignment boundaries approximate but consistent across six comparisons.
